Encore 0.6.1: your session stays signed in, and playback survives a cleared cache.

## Download

| System | File |
|---|---|
| macOS (Apple silicon and Intel) | `Encore_0.6.1_universal.dmg` |
| Windows 10 and 11 | `Encore_0.6.1_x64-setup.exe` (or the `.msi`) |
| Debian 12+, Ubuntu 22.04+ | `Encore_0.6.1_amd64.deb` |
| Other Linux (glibc 2.35+) | `Encore_0.6.1_amd64.AppImage` |

Encore 0.5 and 0.6 update themselves to this version: they download it in
the background and install it the next time you quit, or right away with
**Restart to update**. Updating keeps your session, settings and downloads.
From 0.4 or earlier, download it from this page.

## First launch

These builds are not code-signed yet.

- **macOS:** a fresh download asks you to choose **Open Anyway** in **System
  Settings → Privacy & Security** once. After an update, macOS asks once
  again for access to your saved session in the Keychain; choose **Always
  Allow**.
- **Windows:** SmartScreen warns on first run. Choose **More info**, then
  **Run anyway**. If Smart App Control is on, Windows blocks the app.

## What's new

- **Stay signed in.** Encore now keeps your YouTube session alive the way a
  browser does, so it no longer expires every few hours.
  - A session from **Sign in** is refreshed every few minutes.
  - A session imported from a browser follows that browser: when the
    browser refreshes it, Encore reads it again.
  - On macOS, choose **Always Allow** when asked for the browser's "Safe
    Storage" key, so this happens without asking.

## Fixes

- When YouTube refuses a song because of the session, Encore first refreshes
  the session and tries again. Before, it said the session had expired.
- When macOS or a cleaner app deleted Encore's cache folder while it was
  running, every song failed with "No such file or directory" until a
  restart. Encore now makes the folder again and keeps playing.

Encore is unofficial and not affiliated with YouTube or Google.
